interface.title: GeneRx — Prescribing genes, not just drugs
interface.stage_of_work: Target prioritization: reviewing gene targets already scored by a pipeline that combines Open Targets, ChEMBL and UniProt data
interface.what_it_is_for: Pick a disease and browse its ranked candidate gene targets, how each target's composite score breaks down, which drugs already hit each target, and each target's protein annotation.

data.note: The DuckDB database the app reads was filled with synthetic values by seed_db.py during install. These values stand in for what pipeline.py would produce from the live Open Targets, ChEMBL and UniProt APIs. The genes, scores, tiers, drugs and annotations are illustrative, not real pipeline output. Building a scored target set for a new disease (pipeline.py on EFO IDs) is a command-line step that has to happen before the dashboard, and this run did not exercise it. The seeded database holds two diseases. Type II diabetes mellitus has 14 genes (4 Tier 1, 6 druggable, average OT score 0.641). Breast carcinoma has 5 genes (3 Tier 1, 3 druggable, average OT score 0.748). Breast carcinoma is selected when the app opens. SORT1 and PGR have no UniProt record and no drug. Evolocumab (PCSK9, type II diabetes) and Trastuzumab (ERBB2, breast carcinoma) have a clinical phase but no pChEMBL value.

features.name: Category filter driving a ranked bar chart, a component breakdown and a table
features.general: Choose which score bands to include. A ranked bar chart, a grouped breakdown chart and a data table all redraw on the remaining items. Clearing every band gives an empty state, and 'Select all' restores everything.
features.specific: The Filter by Tier multiselect (Tier1/Tier2/Tier3 chips, Clear all, Select all) filters the Top 20 Biomarkers bar chart, the Score Components chart and the leaderboard table together. The tiers are bands of the composite score.
steps: remove tier chips to narrow the set
reopen the dropdown and add a tier back
Clear all to see the empty state
Select all to restore
serves_tasks: Keep only the highest-scoring band of candidates
See the candidates ranked by overall score

features.name: Score-component grouped bars with legend isolation
features.general: Show each item's sub-scores side by side. Click a legend entry to hide a component, or double-click one to show only that component, so you can compare a single dimension across items.
features.specific: In 'Score Components — Top 10 Genes', ot_score_overall, druggability_score and evidence_richness are grouped per gene. A legend click hides a component, and a double-click shows only that one.
steps: read the grouped bars
click a legend item to hide that component
double-click a legend item to show only it
change the tier filter, which redraws the chart with every component shown again
serves_tasks: Compare how each evidence type contributes to each candidate's score

features.name: Potency-vs-priority scatter with phase pie and linked drug table
features.general: Plot each intervention's measured potency against its target's priority score, with marker size for development stage. Next to it, a pie shows the stage distribution and a table lists every row, including rows with no potency value, which the scatter cannot plot.
features.specific: The Drug Potency vs Biomarker Score scatter (pChEMBL on x, composite score on y, coloured by tier, sized by phase) sits beside the Clinical Phase Distribution pie and above the drug table (drug, target_gene, best_pchembl, max_clinical_phase, assay_type, standard_type).
steps: hover a point for drug, target and phase
drag a box to zoom, double-click to reset
hover the pie for the count per phase
compare the table's row count with the plotted points to find drugs with no potency value
serves_tasks: See each drug's potency against its target's score, and how far the drugs have got in clinical trials
Spot drugs with no potency measurement
Find which existing drug already acts on a given candidate

features.name: Entity picker with metric cards, radar profile and annotation panel
features.general: Choose one item from a type-ahead list to get its headline metrics, a radar of its normalised sub-scores and an annotation panel. Sections the item has no data for are left out.
features.specific: Select Gene (type to filter) fills four metric cards (Composite Score, Tier, OT Score, Clinical Phase), the Evidence Profile radar (OT Score, Druggability, Evidence Richness) and the UniProt Protein Information (name, accession, function, subcellular location, associated diseases).
steps: open Select Gene
type part of a symbol to filter
press Enter or click to choose
read the metric cards and radar, hovering a vertex for its value
read the protein annotation, or see 'None' and 'nan' for unmatched genes
serves_tasks: Open one candidate's profile: headline scores, evidence shape and biological annotation

screens_never_reached: A Gene Detail list limited to the chosen tiers: the Select Gene list always holds every gene for the disease, whatever the tier filter (screens/045.webp)
A drug-tab view filtered by tier: I did not find whether the Tier filter affects Drug Associations. For breast carcinoma every drug-linked gene is Tier1, so the test showed nothing.
not_done: Download as CSV from either table: pressing the button recorded no download in this browser (screens/043.webp shows the drug table's CSV icon hovered). Only the Plotly PNG export saved a file.

Building the scored target set for a new disease (running pipeline.py against new EFO IDs): this prerequisite comes before the dashboard, but the web interface has no control for it. It is a command-line step outside the dashboard.
Viewing two diseases side by side: the app shows one disease at a time, so comparing them meant switching back and forth
Fullscreen, pan and zoom-in/out buttons on the Plotly and table toolbars, the sidebar collapse, and the Streamlit main menu: not tried, because they control the view rather than the science
